steps.title: The grammar G = (V, T, P, S)
steps.explain: A grammar generates strings: start from S and rewrite until only terminals are left. Give all four parts: a list of productions alone is not a grammar.
lines: P has 9 productions: S → aB | bA | ε   A → aS | bAA | a   B → bS | aBB | b

steps.title: What type of grammar is it?
steps.explain: The type is decided by the SHAPE of the productions and nothing else. A Type 3 grammar must be ALL right-linear or ALL left-linear.
lines: S → aB : one variable, at the RIGHT end → right-linear
S → bA : one variable, at the RIGHT end → right-linear
S → ε : terminals only (fits right- and left-linear)
A → aS : one variable, at the RIGHT end → right-linear
A → bAA : two or more variables → context-free only
A → a : terminals only (fits right- and left-linear)
B → bS : one variable, at the RIGHT end → right-linear
B → aBB : two or more variables → context-free only
B → b : terminals only (fits right- and left-linear)
Type 2 (context-free) and not Type 3: A → bAA has two or more variables on the right.
careful: this is the type of the GRAMMAR. Whether the LANGUAGE is regular is a separate question (a Type 2 grammar can generate a regular language)

quiz.question: What is the most restrictive Chomsky type this grammar satisfies?
quiz.why: A → bAA has two or more variables on the right.

steps.title: What each variable generates
steps.explain: Before deriving anything, say what each variable stands for: the set of terminal strings it can turn into. These are the grammar's "facts", and the grammar is correct exactly when they are.
lines: S: exactly the strings with as many a’s as b’s
A: exactly the strings with one more a than b
B: exactly the strings with one more b than a

steps.title: Derive "abba" · step 1 of 4: S → aB
steps.explain: The leftmost variable of S is S. Replace it by aB. In the tree, S gets 2 children, in the same left-to-right order.

quiz.question: S: which production of S comes next, to reach abba?
quiz.why: It gives aB, which can still become abba.

steps.title: Derive "abba" · step 2 of 4: B → bS
steps.explain: The leftmost variable of aB is B. Replace it by bS. In the tree, B gets 2 children, in the same left-to-right order.

quiz.question: aB: which production of B comes next, to reach abba?
quiz.why: It gives abS, which can still become abba.

steps.title: Derive "abba" · step 3 of 4: S → bA
steps.explain: The leftmost variable of abS is S. Replace it by bA. In the tree, S gets 2 children, in the same left-to-right order.

quiz.question: abS: which production of S comes next, to reach abba?
quiz.why: It gives abbA, which can still become abba.

steps.title: Derive "abba" · step 4 of 4: A → a
steps.explain: The leftmost variable of abbA is A. Replace it by a. In the tree, A gets 1 child, in the same left-to-right order.

quiz.question: abbA: which production of A comes next, to reach abba?
quiz.why: It gives abba, which can still become abba.

conclusion: A Type 2 (context-free) grammar. In L(G): abba, ε, ab. Not in L(G): a, b.
